content: Stomatin, also referred to as human erythrocyte integral membrane protein band 7, is a protein encoded by the STOM gene in humans. It is a 31 kDa integral membrane protein that was named after the rare human hemolytic anemia known as hereditary stomatocytosis. This protein is a member of a highly conserved family of integral membrane proteins. It is primarily localized to the cell membrane of red blood cells and other cell types, where it is believed to play a role in regulating ion channels and transporters. A loss of proper localization of stomatin is associated with hereditary stomatocytosis, a specific form of hemolytic anemia. The STOM gene encodes a protein that is widely distributed and constitutively expressed, suggesting that stomatin may have a fundamental role in cellular biology, potentially functioning as a housekeeping protein. Despite this, the precise function of stomatin remains unclear. Its abundant presence in membrane-protruding folds and extensions indicates that it may have a structural role in the formation of these membrane structures or in anchoring them to the actin cytoskeleton.
